title: Roofline (ANALYTICAL) — batch_lm_fusedfd on A100
question: Where does the fused-FD CO kernel sit relative to the A100 hardware ceilings — is it compute-bound, memory-bound, or far below the roofline (latency/occupancy/overhead-bound)? ncu (measured) is blocked by perf-counter permissions, so this is an analytical roofline.
setup: Model FLOPs + DRAM bytes per the fusedfd algorithm (per LM iter, per tree), combine with the MEASURED end-to-end wall time from Tier0. Per-tree op histogram counted exactly from the synth early-gen M=16000 pop; mean iterations from the measured convergence curve. fp32. A100-SXM4-80GB peaks: 19.5 TFLOP/s fp32, 2039 GB/s HBM2e (ridge 9.56 FLOP/byte).

env.ncu: present (/usr/local/cuda/bin/ncu 2024.3.0) but ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM — perf counters admin-locked (RmProfilingAdminOnly=1), no sudo
env.method: ANALYTICAL (modeled FLOP/byte + measured wall); NOT ncu-measured

flop_convention.note: DISCLOSED op-FLOP-equivalent table; ncu would measure real SASS FP instructions

model.dram_bytes_per_iter_per_tree: J write 4*K*N + J read 4*K*N + y writes 8*N + bytecode 12*n + xs(amortized)
model.peaks: fp32 19.5 TFLOP/s, HBM 2039 GB/s, ridge 9.56 FLOP/byte

findings.claim: The kernel sits ~0.5-1% BELOW the A100 ceilings even when saturated — neither compute- nor BW-bound
findings.evidence: Achieved 0.18% (M=16k) -> 0.38% (64k) -> 0.53% of fp32 peak (256k, saturated); 0.33% -> 0.96% of HBM peak. The BW-bound ceiling at AI=5.3 is ~10.8 TFLOP/s; achieved ~0.1 TFLOP/s is ~1% of even that. The binding constraint is execution efficiency / overhead, not the roofline.

findings.claim: Likely bottlenecks (for the optimization work): interpreter divergence + redundancy + host round-trips
findings.evidence: Divergent switch-dispatch tree interpreter; warp-per-tree (32 threads stride N, low ILP, serial stack deps); 1-thread-per-tree K x K Cholesky (terrible occupancy); host-orchestrated LM loop with per-iter H<->D copies + ~8 kernel launches. fd_jacobian re-evaluates the WHOLE tree for each of the K perturbed columns (K full evals/tree/iter) — large redundancy.

findings.claim: If made efficient, the kernel would be (mildly) memory-bound on the J round-trip
findings.evidence: Analytical AI = 5.3 FLOP/byte < ridge 9.56. The dominant modeled DRAM traffic is materializing J (K x N per tree) to global then reading it back in build_jtj. Fusing Jacobian -> JtJ accumulation (never materializing J) would raise AI and cut that traffic.

findings.claim: Achieved fraction rises with utilization, consistent with the throughput sweep
findings.evidence: 0.18% -> 0.53% of peak as M goes 16k -> 256k: more trees fill the 108 SMs, amortizing launch/host overhead — same story as the trees/s-vs-M curve saturating.

plots.caption: Analytical roofline. The 3 fusedfd points (at AI=5.3) sit ~2 orders of magnitude below both the flat compute ceiling and the slanted BW ceiling -> the kernel is bound by execution efficiency/overhead, not by the roofline. Gap = optimization headroom.

caveats: ANALYTICAL, not ncu-measured. FLOPs use a disclosed op-FLOP table (arith=1, div/sqrt=4, transcendental=8); a different convention shifts AI and %-of-peak.

Achieved FLOP/s uses END-TO-END wall time, which includes host orchestration, per-iter H<->D copies, and kernel-launch latency — so it conflates GPU compute with overhead and UNDERSTATES per-kernel GPU efficiency. The 'far below roofline' gap is partly real GPU inefficiency, partly this overhead.
DRAM-byte model counts the J round-trip + y writes + bytecode and assumes xs/bytecode are largely L2-cached (amortized). Real DRAM traffic needs ncu.
mean_iters (12.58) estimated from a 5-iter-resolution convergence curve.
Per-tree distribution is synth early-gen (recoverable problem); late-bloated / inner-const-heavy differ (bigger trees, higher K).
